testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: S-cam drum brake
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What should engine belts NOT have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive wear
questions.explanation: When you inspect your engine, check the belts for tightness and wear. Each belt needs the right amount of tension for your vehicle. Learn what is safe for your specific vehicle.

questions.question: How much water does a road need for a vehicle to hydroplane?
questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on water. It does not take much water on the road for this to happen.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather might mean the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in their car

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving impaired
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs they may be impaired. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, used drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. A driver with their window open in cold weather may be impaired.

questions.question: Do NOT shift gears based on:

options.text: What the vehicle next to you is doing

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer. Learn which gear works best at which speeds for your vehicle. Do not base your decision on other drivers' actions.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Not okay because it can damage your vehicle
Not okay because it confuses other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Not okay because it can damage your vehicle
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and slowly. Rough acceleration can harm your vehicle's parts.

questions.question: What is axle weight?

options.text: The weight one axle puts on the ground
How much the axle itself weighs
The maximum weight an axle can hold

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight one axle puts on the ground
questions.explanation: Axle weight is the weight that one axle or one set of axles puts on the ground.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you would inspect and why
Guess the weight of cargo in a trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you would inspect and why
questions.explanation: During the CDL vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: What can affect your stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on your speed, how heavy your vehicle is, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: 4 psi per minute
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi in a minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern if passengers are not getting off.
Should not be on the road.
Always a concern, even if you cannot see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always a concern, even if you cannot see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around stopped buses. Passengers may walk in front of or behind the bus, and the bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: Fresh oil under your vehicle during a pre-trip inspection means:
questions.correctAnswerText: There is a problem.
questions.explanation: Check under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks before you drive. Any leak is a problem and needs attention.

questions.question: When you swerve to avoid a hazard in a large truck, the danger is that:

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in its lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may flip over.
questions.explanation: Swerving can sometimes be safe, but it has risks. Trucks and trailers sit high and can flip over easily when swerving.

questions.question: Headlights:

options.text: Are usually not needed at night.
Give better light than the sun.
Should be on high beam whenever it is safe and legal.
Should always be on high beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be on high beam whenever it is safe and legal.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night when safe and legal to improve visibility. However, high beams can blind other drivers. Switch to low beams when you are within 500 feet of another vehicle coming toward you.

questions.question: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because:

options.text: The driver may be in a hurry and may not check for other vehicles before leaving.
Packages often fall onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may be in a hurry and may not check for other vehicles before leaving.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because drivers may rush and pull into traffic without looking, or step out suddenly without checking for traffic.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, you should:

options.text: Hold the triangles between your body and oncoming traffic.
Hide the triangles behind your back until you place them.
Hold the triangles as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the triangles between your body and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry the warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic when placing them on the road.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.correctAnswerText: Inside
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are on the wheels and axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are found inside the drum brake.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, you should:

options.text: Exit the road and park safely as soon as you can.
Stop and park where you are.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park safely as soon as you can.
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning light comes on, exit the road and park safely as soon as possible. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well, and you may not be able to stop.

questions.question: Which is NOT a cause of hydraulic brake failure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure happens for two main reasons: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade from overuse on long hills. Downshifting does not cause brake failure.

questions.question: When approaching a curve on the driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Slow down before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down before the curve so you do not need to brake or shift while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The trailer disengages from the tractor.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens on wet roads. Your tires lose grip and slide on the water. This can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time:

options.text: It will probably stay green as you approach.
It is likely to change to yellow soon.
It will skip yellow and go straight to red.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is likely to change to yellow soon.
questions.explanation: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, it will probably turn yellow before you reach it. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful crossing bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system allows poisonous fumes to enter your vehicle. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, you should:

options.text: Look at them for long periods of time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at them briefly.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Be free of cracks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage. Look for cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: In hot weather, spots on the pavement where tar is bleeding:

options.text: Have the same traction as the rest of the road.
Have more traction than the rest of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very slippery.
questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. These spots are very slippery, so watch for them.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not roll backwards.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must not roll backwards when you start from a stop. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see hazards. Headlight glare affects vision. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Which of the following may result in an applicant being denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
They have had a speeding conviction within the previous three years.
They did not answer every question correctly on the hazmat endorsement test.
They did not pass the hazmat endorsement test on the first attempt.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazmat endorsement if you renounce U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, have certain felony convictions, are judged mentally defective, or are committed to a mental institution, or if the TSA considers you a security threat.

questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve on a truck can be used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling back when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when you accelerate on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels spin on a slippery surface, release the accelerator.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight a manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh.
The maximum weight a single vehicle can pull.
The minimum weight a single vehicle must haul.
The maximum weight that can be loaded onto a single trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight a manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh.
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating is the maximum weight the manufacturer allows for a vehicle with its load.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, it means:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, there is a problem in the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: Sending text messages while driving:

options.text: Is allowed if the messages are short.
Is allowed if you are asking your employer a question.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not allowed.
questions.explanation: You are not allowed to send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck is loaded correctly.
questions.explanation: Proper loading is essential for safe truck operation. Bad loading can affect how the truck handles, damage the vehicle, and cause cargo to fall and hurt people.

questions.question: When starting a truck with a trailer, the ABS is not working if:

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, the dashboard lights should come on and then turn off. If the yellow ABS light on the left rear of the trailer stays on, the ABS system is not working properly.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Only needed for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required by law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require you to inspect your vehicle before every trip, no matter how long.

questions.question: If a pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, you should:

options.text: Drive the trip anyway and see a mechanic after.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Avoid using the unsafe part but continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get it fixed right away.
questions.explanation: If a pre-trip inspection finds anything unsafe, you must get it repaired before driving. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their gestures.
questions.explanation: Do not let an aggressive driver provoke you. Ignore their angry gestures, avoid eye contact, and do not try to race them.

questions.question: How often should you stop and take a break while driving to avoid fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours
questions.explanation: Take a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent driver fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: When do spring brakes activate?

options.text: When air pressure drops too low.
When a dashboard control is turned on.
When tires have low tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops too low.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure becomes unsafe. Do not wait for them to activate. Exit the road safely and stop as soon as you see a low pressure warning.

questions.question: If you must drive on the shoulder in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: Stay on the shoulder until you stop completely. Then signal, check mirrors, and merge back into traffic. Do not brake hard on the shoulder above 20 mph. Keep one set of wheels on the pavement if you can.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed going down a downgrade?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increases.
questions.explanation: Gravity causes a vehicle's speed to increase going downhill. Choose a safe speed before entering a downgrade based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: Is a pre-trip vehicle inspection required?

options.text: No, not if you use the vehicle regularly.
No, not for trips under 100 miles.
No, only a mechanic can do it.
Yes, it is required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required by law.
questions.explanation: State and federal law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving.

questions.question: When driving at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear sunglasses.
questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses at night—they reduce your visibility. Keep your eyeglasses clean and scratch-free. Be rested and alert before driving at night.

questions.question: When should you cancel your turn signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: After the turn is completed
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on throughout the entire turn. Cancel it only after you finish turning.

questions.question: When does antifreeze help keep an engine working properly?

options.text: Only when it is cold outside.
In both cold and hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: In both cold and hot weather.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Despite its name, antifreeze is important even in hot weather.

questions.question: What can federal inspectors do if they find your vehicle unsafe?

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix it.
Formally ask you to fix the problems.
Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: Federal or state inspectors can remove an unsafe vehicle from service until all safety problems are fixed.

questions.question: How do you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back straight.
Pull forward to the left, then back straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Park completely within the parking space boundaries.
